es: Escribir una valoración equilibrada de una afirmación sobre salud: razones a favor y en contra con pruebas, y una conclusión con certeza graduada.

teaching.en: Some people say that everyone needs eight glasses of water a day.
teaching.es: Algunas personas dicen que todos necesitan ocho vasos de agua al día.
teaching.explanationEs: Presenta la afirmación atribuida a otros (some people say) antes de evaluarla.
segments: Some people say that everyone needs
eight glasses of water a day.
teaching.audioText: Some people say that everyone needs eight glasses of water a day.

teaching.en: On the one hand, a study found that water helps us stay hydrated.
teaching.es: Por un lado, un estudio descubrió que el agua nos ayuda a mantenernos hidratados.
teaching.explanationEs: On the one hand abre la razón a favor, apoyada en un dato.
segments: On the one hand, a study found
that water helps us stay hydrated.
teaching.audioText: On the one hand, a study found that water helps us stay hydrated.

teaching.en: On the other hand, although water is important, other drinks and food also give us water.
teaching.es: Por otro lado, aunque el agua es importante, otras bebidas y alimentos también nos dan agua.
teaching.explanationEs: Although + hecho contrario: reconoce un punto sin romper el argumento. No se usa con but.
segments: On the other hand, although water is important,
other drinks and food also give us water.
teaching.audioText: On the other hand, although water is important, other drinks and food also give us water.

teaching.en: The evidence is limited, so it depends on the person.
teaching.es: La evidencia es limitada, así que depende de la persona.
teaching.explanationEs: It depends on + persona o situación. Limited evidence: pocas pruebas.
teaching.audioText: The evidence is limited, so it depends on the person.

teaching.en: It is unlikely that everyone needs exactly eight glasses.
teaching.es: Es poco probable que todos necesiten exactamente ocho vasos.
teaching.explanationEs: It is unlikely that + oración: conclusión prudente, no absoluta.
teaching.audioText: It is unlikely that everyone needs exactly eight glasses.

teaching.en: I conclude that the claim is partly true, but it is not a fixed rule.
teaching.es: Concluyo que la afirmación es en parte cierta, pero no es una regla fija.
teaching.explanationEs: I conclude that cierra la valoración con una certeza graduada.
segments: I conclude that the claim is partly true,
but it is not a fixed rule.
teaching.audioText: I conclude that the claim is partly true, but it is not a fixed rule.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase presenta la afirmación sin darla por cierta?

choices.text: Everyone needs eight hours of sleep.
Everyone knows that we all need eight hours of sleep.
Some people say that everyone needs eight hours of sleep.

feedback.es: Some people say atribuye la idea a otros y deja espacio para evaluarla. Las otras dos la dan por cierta.

hint.es: Atribuye la idea a otros: some people say.

origin.text: Vas a evaluar una idea antes de dar tu opinión.

prompt.es: Completa: «Aunque la prueba es limitada, la idea puede ser útil.»

feedback.es: Although introduce el punto contrario sin necesidad de but.

origin.text: ___ the evidence is limited, the idea may be useful.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Por otro lado, la evidencia es limitada.»

answer.text: On the other hand the evidence is limited

feedback.es: On the other hand abre el punto en contra; después va la razón.

hint.es: Empieza con el conector que introduce el lado contrario.

choices.text: It is unlikely that this idea is true for everyone.
This idea is completely false for everyone.

feedback.es: Con pocas pruebas se concluye con it is unlikely that…; las otras dos son absolutas.

origin.text: Has visto pruebas limitadas y quieres concluir con cuidado.

prompt.es: Completa: «Depende de la persona: algunos necesitan más agua que otros.»

feedback.es: Con it el verbo lleva -s: it depends on the person.

origin.text: It ___ on the person: some need more water than others.

prompt.es: Escribe una frase en contra con although.

answer.text: Although the idea is popular, there is no evidence.
accepted: Although the idea is popular, there is no evidence.
There is no evidence, although the idea is popular.

feedback.es: Although reconoce que el mito es popular y aun así el argumento sigue: no hay pruebas.

origin.text: Aunque la idea es popular, no hay pruebas.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige la conclusión del hablante.

choices.text: The effect is not the same for everybody.

feedback.es: El hablante concluye it depends on the person: el efecto cambia según cada uno.

origin.audio: On the one hand, exercise helps the heart. On the other hand, too much exercise can hurt us. So I conclude that it depends on the person.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase reconoce un punto contrario sin usar but?

choices.text: Although the plan is cheap, but it takes a lot of time.
The plan is cheap although, it takes time.
Although the plan is cheap, it takes a lot of time.

feedback.es: Although ya expresa el contraste; añadir but es un error común. La tercera frase coloca mal although.

origin.text: Quieres decir que el plan es barato, pero que requiere mucho tiempo.

prompt.es: Completa: «La evidencia es limitada, así que no podemos estar seguros.»

feedback.es: Pocas pruebas se dice limited evidence, y obliga a concluir con cuidado.

origin.text: The evidence is ___, so we cannot be sure.

prompt.es: Evalúa la afirmación con razones a favor, razones en contra y una conclusión graduada.

answer.text: Some people say that breakfast is the most important meal of the day. On the one hand, a school survey found that students who eat breakfast concentrate better in class. They also have more energy in the morning. On the other hand, the evidence is limited, because most studies only ask people about their habits. Although breakfast helps many students, some people are just not hungry in the morning. I conclude that the claim is partly true, but it depends on the person. It is unlikely that breakfast is equally important for everyone.
accepted: Some people say that breakfast is the most important meal of the day. On the one hand, a school survey found that students who eat breakfast concentrate better in class. They also have more energy in the morning. On the other hand, the evidence is limited, because most studies only ask people about their habits. Although breakfast helps many students, some people are just not hungry in the morning. I conclude that the claim is partly true, but it depends on the person. It is unlikely that breakfast is equally important for everyone.

Some people think that we should do homework every night. On the one hand, a study found that regular practice improves grades. It also helps students learn to organise their time. On the other hand, the evidence is limited, because tired students learn less. Although homework can help, too much of it may hurt sleep. In conclusion, the claim is partly true, but it depends on the student. It is unlikely that the same amount of homework is good for everyone.

feedback.es: Una valoración equilibrada atribuye la afirmación, da razones a favor y en contra con datos y cierra con certeza graduada.

origin.text: Afirmación: «Desayunar es la comida más importante del día.» Escribe unas 90 palabras: atribúyela a otros, da dos razones a favor con un dato, dos en contra con un punto contrario y cierra con una conclusión graduada.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada expresión con su función en la valoración.

feedback.es: Cada expresión marca una parte de la valoración: a favor, en contra, punto contrario y conclusión.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Concluyo que la afirmación es en parte cierta.»

answer.text: I conclude that the claim is partly true

feedback.es: I conclude that abre la conclusión y partly true la gradúa.

prompt.es: Completa: «Es poco probable que un solo estudio demuestre toda la afirmación.»

feedback.es: It is unlikely that… indica una conclusión prudente: hay pocas pruebas.

origin.text: It is ___ that one study proves the whole claim.
